subject.title: [BUG] exec tool: aborted run wedges subsequent exec calls in same session (regression from PR #94412)

question: Is the current production evidence sufficient to route this as part of the run-lifecycle PR track, or do maintainers want a separate focused exec-abort repro before any repair is queued?
rationale: The source and related PRs show plausible owners, but the exact state that wedges subsequent exec calls is not proven and the latest comments suggest the same symptom may surface through broader liveness paths.

options.title: Require focused repro first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a small current-main repro or diagnostic snapshot that distinguishes exec process settlement, reply-run lane release, and diagnostic marker cleanup before queueing a fix.

options.title: Fold into run-lifecycle track
options.body: Treat the issue as covered by the existing run-lifecycle PRs only if maintainers confirm those PRs prove recovery for the reported `tool:exec:started` same-session wedge.

options.title: Queue a narrow exec repair
options.body: Allow an automated repair attempt only for an exec-specific regression test and fix, with instructions to stop if the root cause is broader than exec lifecycle cleanup.

recommendation.title: Require focused repro first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a small current-main repro or diagnostic snapshot that distinguishes exec process settlement, reply-run lane release, and diagnostic marker cleanup before queueing a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the linked abort-loop change and has the strongest current-main routing signal across the implicated agent-loop and exec lifecycle code in this checkout.
